solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One and a hundred is a thousand — that's wrong

definitions.note: a noun here: an error or offence

parts.note: sole means one and only
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone protests that adding one and a hundred cannot possibly make a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical blunder or breach of etiquette is a kind of error, a wrong committed in speech or manners.

clue.text: Swig punch

definitions.meaning: a gulp or swallow of a drink
a hard blow with the fist

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a slurp of liquor, and a heavy hit to someone.

clue.text: Dirty linen evidently washed, disgusting originally

indicators.note: originally means take each word's first letter

explanation.surface: Dirty laundry, clearly washed, was disgusting at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the initials of linen, evidently, washed and disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude, smutty or obscene, the sense of dirty jokes and dirty talk.

clue.text: Singing in Cambridge mansion, roof coming off

parts.note: Cantab is short for Cantabrigian, of Cambridge University

indicators.note: in a down answer the roof is the top letter, removed here

parts.note: a pile is a grand stately house

explanation.surface: Singing in a Cambridge mansion whose roof has blown off.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning in a smooth, flowing, song-like style.

clue.text: Writing tool, magic marker?

parts.note: a spell is magic
a checker marks work, such as an examiner; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: A writing tool that is a magic felt-tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magic marker' looks like the felt pen brand but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that flags misspelt words is an aid for anyone composing text.

clue.text: America on bottom row

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another is written after it

parts.note: the rump is the backside
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: An American sits on the bottom row of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a line of seats but means a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or loud quarrel is a row, rhyming with cow, and that commotion is the sense.

clue.text: Central parts of industry reassuringly, and quietly, appropriate

indicators.note: central parts are the middle two letters of each word

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Core parts of an industry are quietly, reassuringly suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' is the verb, to seize, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something for yourself without right, to seize it, is to appropriate it.

clue.text: There she goes to blunder into catastrophe, captive initially

indicators.note: initially says this piece comes first

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: into puts the blunder inside the catastrophe

parts.note: doom is ruin or catastrophe
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A woman heads off to make a disastrous mistake, a prisoner at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There she goes' is a cryptic pointer to the ladies' room, a euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' toilet, where women go, is a playful reading of 'there she goes'.

clue.text: Enjoyable day is going well, draining lake

parts.note: Sat is Saturday

indicators.note: draining means letting the lake run out

parts.note: flying means going very well
L is lake on maps

explanation.surface: A pleasant day goes well until the lake is drained.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasing and fulfilling gives contentment, near to enjoyable.

clue.text: Single housing worker going begging

indicators.note: one piece housing another holds it inside

parts.note: unwed means unmarried, single
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: An unmarried person shelters a labourer who is out begging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going begging is available because nobody has claimed or wanted it.

clue.text: Be cleverer than foolish undergraduate?

parts.note: OU stands for a university (the Oxford University of a student body, or the Open University), standing in for one of its students
a twit is a foolish person; the question mark admits the stretch from adjective to noun

explanation.surface: A student is so silly that anyone could get the better of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read as 'foolish undergraduate' = an OU TWIT, a university's silly student; the question mark flags the looseness.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone through superior cunning or intelligence is exactly this verb.

clue.text: See about lesser VIP somehow becoming megastar

indicators.note: the see goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity somehow turns into a superstar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese, Ely in Cambridgeshire, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The King of Rock and Roll was one of the biggest stars music has known.

clue.text: Lack of craft, perhaps, about a digital processing instrument

indicators.note: the word for lack goes around the letter A

parts.note: nil means nothing, a lack
clippers are fast sailing ships, an example of craft

explanation.surface: A rant about a lack of craftsmanship in some digital data-processing tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' means to do with fingers, not computers: the tool trims fingernails.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers, so a gadget that processes them by trimming their nails is a cute cryptic description of the tool.

clue.text: A UK citizen holds I require bottles to be drunk

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, around the Briton piece

parts.note: to need is to require

indicators.note: holds puts the letter A inside the citizen

parts.note: a Brit is a British citizen

explanation.surface: A Briton says they need bottles to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoxicated or tipsy from alcohol, the formal word for being drunk.

clue.text: Meaty stuff signalled, a trombone part coming up

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up means reading upwards, backwards
part means a run of letters is found within the words

explanation.surface: A trombone section signalled for some substantial music.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Italian sausage from Bologna, flecked with fat, is meaty stuff.

clue.text: Biblical character I whine about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: to moan is to whine or complain

explanation.surface: Someone admits to complaining about a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth she is Ruth's mother-in-law, a woman of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Bunch attending one musical — and another?

definitions.note: a second musical, after the first one named

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the bunch comes along after the musical

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a spray is a bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: A group of fans go to one musical show, then to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a musical (and film) set in 1960s Baltimore, hence 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: This stage show with songs, based on a John Waters film, is a further example of a musical beyond the first.

clue.text: Post contains rubbish: foolish ultimately opening it

indicators.note: opening it means the letter goes into the anagram just made
rubbish signals the letters are worthless as they stand and must be rearranged
ultimately means the last letter

explanation.surface: A mailbox holds rubbish; a fool finally opens it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' scrambles CONTAINS; 'ultimately' gives H from foolish; 'opening it' puts the H into the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright bar or pole used as a support is a post.

clue.text: Flower — bottom part raised, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for a bottom part is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a buttock is part of the bottom
up means raised

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about a raised backside, posed as a flower riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTOCK said aloud is only loosely like BUTTERC, as the question mark concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow wild bloom of the genus Ranunculus, common in meadows.

clue.text: Deck, where sailors joining a party

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: On a ship's deck, sailors join in a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like part of a ship but is the verb meaning decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to decorate or embellish it, as in deck the halls.

clue.text: Lack of interest concerning argument

parts.note: in can mean concerning, as in 'in the matter of'
a difference is a disagreement or argument

explanation.surface: An argument about something nobody cares about.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy or unconcern is the state of not caring, which a lack of interest describes.

clue.text: Speeding boats

definitions.meaning: a body of ships under one command

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the poetic adjective for swift; the other is a navy's collection of vessels.

clue.text: Without allure, nappies emptied

parts.note: SA is sex appeal, allure

indicators.note: emptied means take out the inside, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: Something without charm: nappies being emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived preposition meaning lacking, as in Shakespeare's 'sans teeth'.

clue.text: A mischievous thing coming up that may irritate?

definitions.text: A mischievous thing coming up that may irritate?

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up reads the letters upwards

parts.note: an elf is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A mischievous creature rising up to annoy someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting insect that may irritate the skin.

clue.text: Marks in Spanish listed when failing

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters collapse into a new order

explanation.surface: Marks in a Spanish exam were listed against failing students.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy accent over an n in Spanish (as in señor) is this diacritic mark.

clue.text: Everything considered, suggesting tall helot?

parts.note: read the solution as an instruction: put ALL inside a synonym of its second ALL, THE LOT (both mean everything), giving T-ALL-HE LOT, which respaced is these two words

explanation.surface: A tall slave of ancient Sparta seems to sum things up.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the solution is the wordplay and the clue's words are what it builds. A helot was a Spartan serf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning on the whole, taking all aspects together.

clue.text: Want relief primarily in the end

indicators.note: in puts the opening letter inside the word for the end

parts.note: death is the end of life

indicators.note: primarily means take only the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone wanting relief first and foremost, at the end of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' is a noun: scarcity, not desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity or shortage of something is a want of it.

clue.text: Where to work out if reliability's back in faulty gas main

indicators.note: in places the final letter within the rearranged pipe letters
faulty signals that the letters are wrongly assembled
back means take the hindmost letter of reliability

explanation.surface: A worry about how reliable a faulty gas main is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives Y, the last letter of reliability; 'faulty' scrambles GAS MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyms are halls for physical exercise, the places where people work out.
